pages.title: CEO Statement
pages.name: Lisa Jackson
pages.role: VP, Environment, Policy and Social Initiatives
pages.header: At Apple, we are constantly innovating to make the world's best technology while reducing our impact on the environment.
paragraphs: Every year, teams across our company find new and innovative ways to make our technology better for people and the planet. That progress has brought us closer than ever to Apple 2030: our goal to become carbon neutral for our global footprint, including our supply chain and the energy our customers use to power their devices.

Thanks to these efforts, I'm proud to share that Apple has now cut our overall emissions by more than 60 percent since 2015. This report covers the work that makes a milestone like that possible. It describes in detail how we continue to dramatically reduce our climate impact, while helping accelerate a global transition toward recycled materials and renewable energy.

Since 2018, we've powered every Apple facility with renewable energy — including our offices, retail stores, and data centers. That progress is quickly making its way across our global supply chain, and today, our suppliers now support more than 17.8 gigawatts of clean energy around the world.

To drive down carbon emissions even further, we're using more recycled materials than ever before. We now use 99 percent recycled rare earth elements in the magnets across our products. We've also continued to scale the use of recycled materials like tungsten, aluminum, cobalt, gold, and lithium.

In October, we unveiled our latest carbon neutral product, Mac mini, which is made with more than 50 percent recycled content and manufactured with electricity exclusively sourced from renewable energy. That's helped reduce the carbon footprint of Mac mini by 80 percent from our business-as-usual scenario.
At Apple, we've always believed that innovation is a powerful force for progress. So we'll continue to do our part to protect the planet — and to build a better future for generations to come.

pages.title: Overview
pages.intro: Apple has reduced its entire carbon footprint by more than 60 percent compared with its 2015 baseline — without offsets. During the same period, revenue grew by more than 65 percent. Our goal is carbon neutrality across our entire footprint by 2030.

pillars.title: Apple 2030
pillars.body: 75% gross emissions reduction by 2030 vs 2015. Science Based Targets initiative validated. Carbon neutral for corporate operations since 2020.

pillars.title: Electricity
pillars.body: 100% renewable energy for all Apple facilities since 2018. Suppliers generated 31.3 million MWh of clean energy in FY2024.

pillars.title: Design & Materials
pillars.body: 24% of materials shipped in products from recycled sources. 99% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.

pillars.title: Resources
pillars.body: Freshwater replenishment: 40% achieved toward 100% by 2030. Corporate waste diversion rate: 70%. Zero landfill at all final assembly sites.

pages.title: Climate & Emissions
body: Apple has reduced its entire carbon footprint by more than 60 percent compared with its 2015 baseline — without offsets. During the same period, revenue grew by more than 65 percent. The goal is a 75 percent reduction in gross emissions by 2030, after which remaining emissions will be balanced with high-quality carbon removals to reach full carbon neutrality.

In 2024 alone, environmental programs avoided 41 million metric tons of emissions — led by supplier clean energy transitions (21.8M mt), direct emissions abatement (8.4M mt), and low-carbon materials (6.2M mt).
pages.footnote: Gross emissions cover scopes 1, 2, and 3. Net emissions = gross minus carbon offsets/removals. Avoided emissions estimated vs. a business-as-usual scenario. Source: Apple Environmental Progress Report, Fiscal Year 2024.

pages.title: Energy & Renewables
pages.header: renewable energy for all Apple facilities since 2020
body: Apple's retail stores, data centers, and offices around the world source 100 percent renewable electricity. The Supplier Clean Energy Program has driven suppliers to generate 31.3 million MWh of clean energy in FY2024, supporting 17.8 gigawatts of capacity worldwide.

The Supplier Energy Efficiency Program has achieved more than 2.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity savings since 2015. In FY2024, Apple facilities saved 298,358 MWh per year from efficiency measures.

kpis.label: Annual savings from Apple efficiency program, FY2024

pages.title: Water & Waste
body: Apple is committed to replenishing all corporate freshwater withdrawals in high-stress locations by 2030. The company has achieved 40% of that goal to date. The Supplier Clean Water Program saved 14 billion gallons of freshwater in FY2024, with participating sites averaging a 42% water reuse rate.
Corporate waste diversion reached 70% in FY2024. Zero waste to landfill has been maintained at all established final assembly sites since 2018.

Landfill at all final assembly sites (since 2018)

pages.footnote: Water data covers corporate facilities. Supply chain water footprint tracked separately via Clean Water Program. Source: Apple Environmental Progress Report, Fiscal Year 2024.

pages.title: Product Lifecycle
body: Apple designs products for durability, repairability, and recovery from the earliest stages. The iPhone 16 introduced a new low-voltage battery removal process. Repair Assistant, launched with iOS 18, allows configuration of new and used Apple parts directly on device. Parts availability extends up to 7 years, with Mac laptop battery repair available for up to 10 years.

In FY2021, Apple sent 12.2 million devices and accessories to new owners for reuse via trade-in programs in 25 countries. The Daisy robot disassembles up to 23 iPhone models; Dave recovers tungsten and rare earth elements from Taptic Engines; Taz recycles modules containing rare earth magnets.

features.title: Durability
features.body: Products tested against strict durability standards mimicking real-world conditions. Ceramic Shield glass 50% tougher than first generation. IP68 water resistance across flagship lineup.

features.title: Repairability
features.body: Parts available up to 7 years post-sale. Mac laptop battery repair up to 10 years. Over 5,000 AASP locations and 3,000+ Independent Repair Providers worldwide. Self Service Repair launched 2022.

features.title: Material recovery
features.body: Daisy disassembles up to 23 iPhone models. Dave recovers tungsten, rare earth elements, and steel from Taptic Engines. Taz recycles rare earth magnet modules.

features.title: Product carbon footprint
features.body: iPhone 16: 56–97 kg CO₂e depending on configuration. MacBook Air 15-inch (M4): 147–155 kg CO₂e. Full LCA certified to ISO 14040/14044 by Fraunhofer Institute.

pages.title: Material
pages.header: Transitioning to recycled and renewable materials
body: In 2024, 24 percent of the materials shipped in Apple products came from recycled sources. Apple is committed to one day using only recycled or renewable materials. Key FY2024 milestones: 99% recycled tungsten, 99% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 76% recycled cobalt, 71% recycled aluminum, 53% recycled lithium, 40% recycled gold.
Packaging plastic has been reduced by more than 75% since 2015. In FY2024, fiber transitions avoided 1,700 metric tons of plastic. The goal is to remove all plastics from packaging by end of 2025.

kpis.label: Recycled rare earth elements in all magnets
Plastic avoided via fiber packaging transitions (FY2024)

pages.footnote: Material percentages reflect certified recycled content and supplier-reported data. Packaging data from Apple Environmental Progress Report FY2024.

pages.title: Our People
pages.header: Creating an inclusive, safe and supportive environment
body: With over 164,000 team members worldwide, Apple's people are at the heart of everything we do. Since 2017, Apple has achieved and maintained gender pay equity for employees worldwide. In the U.S., pay equity has also been achieved with respect to race and ethnicity — as well as at the intersections of race, ethnicity and gender.

In calendar year 2021, 47% of open leadership roles were filled by women globally — a 10 percentage point increase from 2020. Apple's more than 15,000 managers receive training in unconscious bias and inclusive leadership. 185,000 hours of inclusion and diversity training were delivered in calendar year 2021.

leadership.title: Open leadership roles filled — calendar year 2021

payEquity.header: Pay equity across every dimension, in every country
payEquity.intro: Since 2017, Apple has achieved and maintained gender pay equity for all employees worldwide. In the U.S., pay equity has also been achieved with respect to race and ethnicity — as well as at their intersections with gender. An independent third-party expert builds and runs statistical models annually to assess and resolve any differences in total compensation.

programs.title: Annual pay equity review
programs.body: Independent third-party expert assesses total compensation — base salary, bonus, and stock — on the basis of gender globally, and race and ethnicity in the U.S., resolving any differences found.

programs.title: No salary history policy
programs.body: Apple does not ask candidates for salary history during recruiting — a global policy since 2019. Offers are based on compensation of current Apple employees in similar roles.

programs.title: Annual compensation planning
programs.body: The People team uses analytics to assess promotion rates, performance rating distribution, and pay metrics for women vs. men and, in the U.S., for underrepresented groups vs. non-underrepresented groups.

pages.title: Community
pages.header: A force for equity and opportunity
body: Apple's Racial Equity and Justice Initiative (REJI) began in June 2020 with an initial commitment of $100 million. Additional commitments of $30 million (August 2021) and $25 million (May 2022) brought the total to $155 million+. REJI focuses on education access, criminal justice reform, and removing economic barriers for communities of color.

Apple's Employee Giving program celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2021, having raised nearly $725 million for 39,000 organizations worldwide. Over $120 million was distributed in FY2021 alone. 68,000 employees have logged almost 2 million volunteer hours since 2011.

initiatives.title: Racial Equity & Justice Initiative
initiatives.body: $155M+ committed since 2020. Propel Center for HBCU community, HSI Innovation Hub (Cal State Northridge), HBCU C2 Initiative at 45 campuses. Criminal justice reform and $75M in economic empowerment commitments.

initiatives.title: Community Education Initiative
initiatives.body: 147 partner institutions including 47 HBCUs across 500+ locations in 36 U.S. states and UK. Apple Developer Academy: 23 programs in 7 countries, 15,000+ graduates since 2013, 92% alumni employment rate.

initiatives.title: Employee Giving
initiatives.body: Nearly $725 million raised for 39,000 organizations since 2011. 45,000+ employee donors in FY2021. Dollar-for-dollar matching up to $10,000 per employee per year, raised to 2:1 in times of need.

initiatives.title: Affordable Housing
initiatives.body: $2.5 billion commitment to address housing in California. $1 billion+ deployed across 25+ counties as of July 2021. Veterans Square (Pittsburg, CA): 30-unit 100% free housing for local veterans.

pages.title: Supply Chain
pages.header: People first across our entire supply chain
body: Apple's supply chain spans 3 million+ people across thousands of businesses and facilities in 52 countries. The Supplier Code of Conduct and Supplier Responsibility Standards — updated annually, published in 15 languages since 2005 — set requirements across labor and human rights, health and safety, environment, ethics, and management systems.

In FY2021, 1,177 assessments were conducted in 52 countries including 211 unannounced visits — nearly double the prior year. Since 2008, more than 23.6 million supplier employees have been trained on their workplace rights. Suppliers have directly repaid $33.2 million in recruitment fees to 37,322 workers since 2008.

programs.title: Worker Voice
programs.body: 352,589 supplier employees directly engaged via interviews and satisfaction surveys in FY2021 — nearly double the prior year. Anonymous third-party hotlines available in any language, 24/7. 22% increase in hotline utilization following awareness campaign.

programs.title: Forced Labor Prevention
programs.body: Zero tolerance for forced labor. 1,100+ assessments in FY2021 — zero instances of forced labor found. Responsible Labor Recruitment Toolkit deployed to 39+ facilities in 10 countries, reaching ~77,000 workers.

programs.title: Education & Development
programs.body: $50 million Supplier Employee Development Fund announced March 2022. 5 million supplier employees have benefited from learning programs since 2008. New Apple Education Hub launching in U.S., China, India, and Vietnam.

pages.title: Board & Leadership
pages.header: A diverse, independent board overseeing ESG at the highest level
body: Apple's Board of Directors, assisted by its standing committees, has ultimate responsibility for oversight of significant risks — including environmental, social, and governance matters. The full Board directly oversees Apple's Human Rights Policy implementation and environmental goals and initiatives.

More than half of Board members identify as women and/or members of Asian, Black, Hispanic/Latinx, LGBTQ+, and veterans communities. Women hold half of Board and committee leadership positions. The Compensation Committee incorporated an ESG Modifier into executive annual cash incentives beginning in 2021, based on progress across Apple's six core values.

committees.name: Audit and Finance Committee
committees.esgRole: Oversees Green Bond Impact reporting, privacy & data security risks, enterprise risk management. Reviews tax matters and financial reporting.

committees.name: Compensation Committee
committees.esgRole: ESG Modifier incorporated into executive annual cash incentive program since 2021, covering accessibility, education, environment, inclusion & diversity, privacy, and supplier responsibility.

committees.name: Nominating & Corporate Governance Committee
committees.esgRole: Board composition and governance practices. Director independence and succession planning.

pages.title: Risk & Compliance
pages.header: Enterprise risk management integrated with ESG
body: Apple's Enterprise Risk Management Program identifies, assesses, monitors, manages, and mitigates significant business risks — including financial, operational, compliance, and reputational risks. A Risk Oversight Committee composed of the CFO, General Counsel, Head of Business Assurance, and senior business leaders reports to the Audit and Finance Committee.

In 2021, key focus areas included health and safety, environment, people, privacy and data security, supply chain and operations, and legal and regulatory risks including antitrust. Apple conducted a TCFD-aligned climate scenario analysis in 2020, considering a range of future scenarios including below 2°C.

riskAreas.name: Climate transition risk
riskAreas.body: TCFD-aligned scenario analysis conducted in 2020. Apple 2030 roadmap directly addresses climate transition risks. Carbon pricing and regulatory changes tracked continuously across all regions of operation.

riskAreas.name: Supply chain & human rights
riskAreas.body: 1,177 supplier assessments in FY2021 across 52 countries including 211 unannounced visits. ESCI team within Worldwide Operations reports to senior management. Human Rights Policy overseen directly by Board of Directors.

riskAreas.name: Privacy & data security
riskAreas.body: ISO 27001 and ISO 27018 certified with yearly audits. Audit and Finance Committee regularly reviews privacy and data security risks. Chief Privacy Officer reports to SVP and General Counsel, who chairs the Privacy Steering Committee.

riskAreas.name: Regulatory & antitrust
riskAreas.body: Anti-corruption, antitrust, export/sanctions, and third-party compliance programs. Third-party compliance program rated 'mature and leading practice' by two external parties. 98% employee training completion in FY2021.

riskAreas.name: Reputational risk
riskAreas.body: EthicsPoint third-party reporting service available 24/7, multilingual, anonymous where legally permitted. Business Conduct Helpline for employees and external parties. Annual independent program assessments.

pages.title: Ethics & Transparency
pages.header: Conducting business with integrity and full transparency
body: Apple's Business Conduct Policy guides ethical requirements for all employees — available in over 20 languages. It covers honesty, respect, confidentiality, and compliance. All employees complete an annual scenario-based online Business Conduct training updated each year. In FY2021, 98% of employees completed this training, representing 902,000 Apple training courses and 432,000 hours.

Apple does not make political contributions to individual candidates or parties and has no political action committee. Since February 2016, Apple has issued a total of $4.7 billion in green bonds — the November 2019 issuance of €2 billion was Apple's first green bond in Europe.

hero.headline: We've reduced our emissions by over 60%
hero.body: This milestone brings us closer than ever to our 2030 commitment — to become carbon neutral across our entire global footprint by using more recycled materials, renewable electricity, and lower-carbon transportation.

impactNumbers.heading: A decade of measurable progress
body: Since 2015, we have systematically transformed how we operate — from the energy we use to the materials we source and the communities we serve. These numbers represent real change, not targets.
Every metric is independently verified and reported against the GRI Standards framework, ensuring full transparency with our stakeholders.
